data.narrative:
Vast is a seed-stage space and aerospace company founded by Jed McCaleb that has raised $300M+. The valuation exercise draws from a universe of 6 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX and Rocket Lab, though the private set lacks sufficient homogeneous clustering for narrow peer-median analysis.

A single applicable method—stage-progression—anchors this analysis. Using $26M as a proxy for total capital raised and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $65M. The public-comp anchoring method is inapplicable because Vast's revenue is not disclosed; while the Space & Aerospace sector median trades at 24.4x revenue across the 5-ticker public set, this multiple cannot be meaningfully applied without the target's top-line figure.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $55M to $75M, with a central estimate of $65M. This range reflects limited method coverage—only stage-progression provides a quantitative anchor. Key uncertainties include (1) the actual capital deployment and burn pattern underlying the $300M+ raised total; (2) Vast's current revenue run-rate, which would enable public-multiple triangulation; and (3) the applicability of early-stage step-up multiers to a heavily capitalized seed-stage business, which may follow atypical financing trajectories.
